title: Stored x-only leaf birthday search on secp256k1 at 125.307122443963: six leaves per batched inverse, keyed by B times the canonical x (pi = A + B*omega, secp256k1's Frobenius), with a range-local K2 scan

claims.statement: For uniform production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold stored-leaf birthday search of proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.390000001 over the challenge and fresh algorithm coins, with no heuristic: the Chen-Stein method on cross-node leaf pairs bounds P(no collision), and drops, caps, wrong class indices and the enumerated inline-carry sites of the kernels (section 3.4) are charged failure rows, while RNDR, the ideal coin source, adds none (section 6). On every run its total work is at most 2^125.307122443963 target-group-operation equivalents (1000 AArch64 instructions per unit). Each pair of generator points X, Y gives six leaves, the x-coordinates of phi^t(X) + Y and phi^t(X) - Y for t = 0, 1, 2, from one batched inverse of y_Y^2 - y_X^2 (section 3.1). A leaf's key is K = B*min(x, beta x, beta^2 x) mod p, where pi = A + B*omega with A^2 - AB + B^2 = p is secp256k1's Frobenius: as B*beta = A - B and B*beta^2 = -A (mod p), a leaf of class index j computes K as one product of x by a constant below 2^129 and a fold exact outside a set of about 2^-187 per leaf (KCOM, or KNEG for j = 2, which a meter counts), and KEY drops no leaf: a wrong index, on a set of rate below 2^-54.29, gives the key of another member of the leaf's class, a charged missed collision and never a false match (section 3.3). Machine (section 2.1): 2^72 nodes, each with one processor (base AArch64 with FEAT_RNG and FEAT_LSE) and a memory below 2^64 bytes, whose links deliver a message's four words at the address its sender stored and keep no flags, rings or counters. Beyond its sender's instructions, every message's charge includes 8 instruction-equivalents at each hop: its delivery as route.s dlv (6), which the experiment executes for every message of its 4 x 4 run, and its port's in-flight count (2). Hop 1, hop 2 and grouping are charged 18, 18.25 and 18.125 per record; the grouping's scan_ranges compares K2 only, within each d4 range, at 29/8 per record plus at most 23 per range, and its extra 184-bit partial matches are charged to the candidate, request and relay caps (2^28, 2^29, 2^30; section 6.4). certificate.py gives at most 380.9916 instructions per leaf and the claim 125.307122443963. Peak memory at most 2^135.9988 bytes; preprocessing at most 2^110.2061 units, included; no advice; certificate.py checks that the work, memory and preprocessing figures are the least 12-decimal (work) or 4-decimal (memory, preprocessing) values at or above their exact values, and that 0.390000001 is below the success bound. The bound is for the machine of section 2.1. Lineage: our f9d5a673 (transport and grouping) and b3716a20 (the six-leaf fwd and bwd kernels, the site table and the success argument), package 8f733826 (field rows, fe_inv, class row, a64.py), submissions 3828873f, 6ef3e7b3, d637fb0a, 9798f5f4 and d9e3dbf4 (STADD, paired scan comparisons, prefix4, the generator and candidate allowances, a claim on a decimal grid), 472226d8, 4fdb8a9c and e1ecd7cc (a success target nearer 0.39, a 12-decimal claim) and 80e9e8af and 1efcef88 (the range-local scan with its 184-bit accounting and caps); the Frobenius key is new here; no prior acceptance or score is a premise. This is an analytic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the six-leaf kernels on production points, with every leaf's Frobenius class key against B times its canonical x, and the emit, both hops (each message delivered by executing dlv) and the grouping (with scan_ranges) on a 4 x 4 machine, against exact references; check the arithmetic sites of section 3.4, including both key paths; compare the counts of the leaf, inversion, transport, delivery and grouping kernels with certificate.py; run the q25 toy (toy.py) with six leaves per incidence and certificate.py. Budget-limited parts run stated minimums. Not a production-scale attack.
